newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA JOIN INTER AND SAMP IN CHAMPIONS LEAGUE RACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA JOIN INTER AND SAMP IN CHAMPIONS LEAGUE RACE.

text.p: Parma joined Inter and Sampdoria on Sunday in what now looks like a race to finish second in Serie A behind pace-setters Juventus and claim a berth in next season's European Cup.

Juventus, who look destined to celebrate their 100th anniversary year with a record 24th league title, tightened their grip on the championship on Saturday with a 2-0 victory over Italian Cup finalists Vicenza in Turin.
That left them seven points clear of Inter and Parma and eight ahead of Sampdoria, who could have cut the gap but lost 2-1 at home to Bologna instead.
For the first time, the league runner-up will be guaranteed a place in the Champions League next season and that race at least remains wide-open.
Inter remain in pole position after Saturday's 3-0 win at Piacenza in which goalkeeper Gianluca Pagliuca saved a first-half penalty and England's Paul Ince scored twice.
But Parma pressed their claims with a 3-2 victory over struggling Cagliari.

Carlo Ancelotti's side, recovering strongly from a slow start to the season, turned round 2-0 up after goals from France's Lilian Thuram and Hernan Crespo - only his second since joining Parma from Argentine club River Plate.
Within five minutes of the break, Crespo scored a third with a spectacular bicycle kick and Parma were coasting to victory.
But Sandro Tovalieri pulled a goal back in the 73rd and then made the home side pay for Enrico Chiesa's 88th minute penalty miss with a second in the 89th before time ran out for Cagliari.
When Vincenzo Montella gave Sampdoria the lead against Bologna in the 22nd minute with his 14th goal of the season, the Genoa side looked like cutting Juve's lead to five points.
But in a remarkable comeback, Bologna shook off the after-effects of last week's Italian Cup semi-final defeat to Vicenza to inflict the Genoa side's second successive home loss.

First, Russian striker Igor Kolyvanov - suspended for the Cup defeat - thundered home a tremendous 25-metre freekick; then, in the 90th minute, the same striker was on hand to beat Fabrizio Ferron from close range for the winner.
Samp were left to rue the post which denied Argentine Juan Veron in the ninth minute and Marco Carparelli's failure to score when clean through in the 85th minute.

Milan are languishing in 11th place after dropping valuable points in a 1-1 home draw with Roma, and could fall back further after Udinese play Napoli later, but president Silvio Berlusconi refused to give up hope of qualifying for Europe.
"We can still make it," said Berlusconi after another disappointing performance from the reigning champions.

It said much about Milan's form that Pietro Vierchowod, at 37 the oldest player in Serie A, rather than Roberto Baggio or George Weah, was on hand to punish lacklustre Roma defending and put the home side in front in the 65th minute.
At this stage, Roma manager Carlos Bianchi sent on Daniel Fonseca and the Uruguay international responded with a headed equaliser in the 75th minute.
At Bergamo, Perugia fought back bravely from Marco Sgro's 75th minute opener with a penalty from Federico Giunti in the 83rd minute and Marco Negri's effort three minutes later.
But Gianluigi Lentini, once the world's most expensive player and back to his best after a car accident almost four years ago, conjured an equaliser out of nothing in the 88th.
Bottom-of-the-table Reggiana registered only their second win of the season with a 4-2 triumph at fellow strugglers Verona in which Russian Igor Simutenkov was on target twice.
